The [Coworker.org Bossware and Employment Tech Database](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk) catalogs more than 550 labor-focused technology products used to monitor, track, and manage workers across various industries. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk)]
What is Bossware?
"Bossware" refers to software and digital tools that managers use to supervise employee habits, outputs, physical locations, and biometrics. Common features include: [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiQEB6zswFS0-snMTwcg4NpgoMLj2V4Ea6xuE2BoqDEdUvY6WUVOulYKikvVb1rTZF5gjUgyQjxMaI6v1BfVKQmXFmkRxLe20HJGeYUSu1_nOK1V67XokFDVdSNBssbA2V2uWeNX1MOl16HM73KfBWnRJxJwMPp_UUk4CdTivU2M5YSv1Wz_fs76r8g)]

* Activity Tracking: Logging keystrokes, mouse movements, active window focus, and app or website usage. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV5tkP6OC1JbBCjQ27X-30JNlXuashIscJz3iC4vjxZxnWb8cucZacml5aFem5bYbgI72LKZEb8hPn3cE5tVmk0swvmx36CYT-4_ywib3r9DCbw2UU2s3a9KMCbeuZmB4QsrQE), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVFtGFR7wsbcmhqcb32icrqai1hKTCTiQEb04PHH-doP0F2qGCFWoXdEuc7FF2J_ZL4VQ1_5XqfhZx-gFVVn_nxO7k3WSOcKGx2-In88XZs4lRGoNr0htmGiTsYD85)]
* Visual Monitoring: Taking periodic or continuous screenshots and recording webcams. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVFtGFR7wsbcmhqcb32icrqai1hKTCTiQEb04PHH-doP0F2qGCFWoXdEuc7FF2J_ZL4VQ1_5XqfhZx-gFVVn_nxO7k3WSOcKGx2-In88XZs4lRGoNr0htmGiTsYD85), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV5tkP6OC1JbBCjQ27X-30JNlXuashIscJz3iC4vjxZxnWb8cucZacml5aFem5bYbgI72LKZEb8hPn3cE5tVmk0swvmx36CYT-4_ywib3r9DCbw2UU2s3a9KMCbeuZmB4QsrQE)]
* Location & Biometrics: Tracking real-time GPS locations, facial recognition, or physical movement metrics. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYgHrOzAVUHYEx-lV6_aYvQVA9eV7JVfh8iraMoIm_3K8EWHTOC6zyaee48OyLMVwYh9FYLGIIXv9ozX-_xuqaVjU0l8yNUA63OahxBTOjghpoH3axgsUu-tTiTjvUY0Ca1M7), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk)]
* Productivity Scoring: Generating automated daily scores or flagged alerts for "productive" versus "unproductive" behavior. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESxwEB6zswFSE8JHQhAgqEjHzXEc_tAVYFLpak-BYfhaxcAFb8DzmPFc0x-aUtplN_4YL49sEjALWVLvqsWJqJeC-NjWzWstfLWF8Nq324FxWeGdi2h4NQXyrKd9mPfGYW3ggpY95k_1v75KKdTVyAkznBa2JJutZZGPlmt3TsmXuVBdF7kZCX34cc9NOnOQZZjd7i94FSLZGEWO0GbUet2wINKudR3f1B5ggvQa17i1Pp9wvE-9JckIyxZcBebqiOL6xYLekqcQ5x), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV5tkP6OC1JbBCjQ27X-30JNlXuashIscJz3iC4vjxZxnWb8cucZacml5aFem5bYbgI72LKZEb8hPn3cE5tVmk0swvmx36CYT-4_ywib3r9DCbw2UU2s3a9KMCbeuZmB4QsrQE)]

Key Database Examples
The [Coworker Worktech Database](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk) tracks a wide range of platforms across categories: [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk)]

* Productivity & Monitoring Software: ActivTrak, Hubstaff, Time Doctor, Desklog, and Controlio. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEB6zswFVa21XY9ZhOP6Te1ET-d17IJuVUeUWbDkkYagTPz9o7VbTrGZdOYa-O8twfioQvoK9IpgMBMLIJehifquvYtWl8kPIJo4_lrm_pSTETP4xDt1Blxi3ASMcCae_1vlQoFDsJYPkv-X7nCrowKZaFw5-avfRp79LpYIH-vkrs8MI7qWZ7ylXq_hRJnUPov8be_), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaQHrOzAVudb3HhE81_C8In65UNOHsKsrIySzrq9Xyh1h_hYdEPmTTMw2XAFiJeNlsHvFC0eV75fJI3rA4KuYwrkl_Z6Pxh6pUE21efj2PydC0U6r6dTdfRsGLCgmdaYuCM839URYyYNiIA)]
* Industry-Specific & Logistics Tracking: Amazon internal tools (such as Project Ultraviolet, Mentor App, and WiFi Tracking), Alice Housekeeping (hotel worker tracking), and Netradyne (fleet/driver monitoring). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk)]
* Hiring & AI Analytics: HireVue (voice and interview analysis), Arctic Shores (behavioral hiring assessments), and Arya (AI recruiting). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWwHrOzAVEvr5fP2qQFkcDJb1eLdl701B6pP0ma8N9pi9GAQF413qwEULfWshIHh9ORYdPoR7RN42K5b_zvy8SX1bAQpSBnktY_Oe8Lv6WvQLIr2Yki3PgFY4VEk), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESxwEB6zswFSE8JHQhAgqEjHzXEc_tAVYFLpak-BYfhaxcAFb8DzmPFc0x-aUtplN_4YL49sEjALWVLvqsWJqJeC-NjWzWstfLWF8Nq324FxWeGdi2h4NQXyrKd9mPfGYW3ggpY95k_1v75KKdTVyAkznBa2JJutZZGPlmt3TsmXuVBdF7kZCX34cc9NOnOQZZjd7i94FSLZGEWO0GbUet2wINKudR3f1B5ggvQa17i1Pp9wvE-9JckIyxZcBebqiOL6xYLekqcQ5x)]

Privacy and Data Concerns
Research highlighted by institutions like [Vanderbilt Law School](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEB6zswFVa21XY9ZhOP6Te1ET-d17IJuVUeUWbDkkYagTPz9o7VbTrGZdOYa-O8twfioQvoK9IpgMBMLIJehifquvYtWl8kPIJo4_lrm_pSTETP4xDt1Blxi3ASMcCae_1vlQoFDsJYPkv-X7nCrowKZaFw5-avfRp79LpYIH-vkrs8MI7qWZ7ylXq_hRJnUPov8be_) shows that many workplace monitoring apps collect deep data profiles (including personal emails, device data, and location records) and share them with third-party tech and advertising domains. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEB6zswFVa21XY9ZhOP6Te1ET-d17IJuVUeUWbDkkYagTPz9o7VbTrGZdOYa-O8twfioQvoK9IpgMBMLIJehifquvYtWl8kPIJo4_lrm_pSTETP4xDt1Blxi3ASMcCae_1vlQoFDsJYPkv-X7nCrowKZaFw5-avfRp79LpYIH-vkrs8MI7qWZ7ylXq_hRJnUPov8be_)]

Key Features of the Tracker

* Global Coverage: Tracks policy developments, laws, and agreements across more than 30 countries (including Australia, China, Italy, the United States, and others). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVgHrOzAVMzivhh8Fx5LPsPYXFR5ge-9peJ4YrM1aIISl2yIvE357_4MAstTXc8GJa_VQyeGp1Wh0rFO_LxXVtDz9-9mmML5_U5YbB0aQHUdol0zdh0NQ), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESxAEB6zswFRfsmthFwKWaCO8Kz20zYVWWWAcffd4zNM5wdPxmbqGfPtqNjBjBOGUMygtMhLOT5svXxLDdtMAu8hS8QkI31TwjZJ1nOXZ950dzjxsqmq5QnSs4GkxN1FZl1Suyz_5DpTxboMaaw8MQ8jo2O-jgDLy78kFJSqeXtLbW8LSW5XMK0m0hoDD1evlFjdfMKOru0bJZE3zi_m3mu5VU5IjW5JslFctxlC_-J6CxmGTPI0e0MH5WYq3cgYT7m1E06Vs-)]
* Core Issues Monitored:
   * Employment status classification
   * Remuneration and fair pay
   * Algorithms and automated decision-making
   * Working time
   * Privacy and data protection
   * Occupational safety and health (OSH)
   * Contract termination and account deactivation
   * Collective bargaining [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEB6zswFYd3sAdAYMs3YdPGrqcmfvVRVnS59wEtI5F4H2muDhNtagfBjM3eKlTvBwo6bA2y9ie-bHXqA0gVN1UG9Pdd90u1nDXeawjAIofYWT4Lelg5tuJQHtRnU94zagDx2CotgVwacFAqwPk8Sh7-6_dV5aMd-Vl2FKT24T5sFxyGme-cufnlbnTxWvevmnZbFmfhIw)]
* Target Audience: Built for governments, employers' and workers' representatives, policymakers, and researchers to support evidence-based policymaking. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEB6zswFYd3sAdAYMs3YdPGrqcmfvVRVnS59wEtI5F4H2muDhNtagfBjM3eKlTvBwo6bA2y9ie-bHXqA0gVN1UG9Pdd90u1nDXeawjAIofYWT4Lelg5tuJQHtRnU94zagDx2CotgVwacFAqwPk8Sh7-6_dV5aMd-Vl2FKT24T5sFxyGme-cufnlbnTxWvevmnZbFmfhIw)]

* Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193): Adopted as the first international labour standard to promote decent work and protect digital platform workers.

transcript:
Negotiating a tech offer means treating the total compensation package—not just the base salary—as a flexible starting point.

Core Rules of Tech Negotiation

• Don't say a number first: Avoid sharing your current compensation or salary expectations early in the process. Ask the recruiter for the role’s budgeted band instead.
• Buy time: Never accept or reject an offer on the initial phone call. Respond neutrally with excitement, then ask to review the details in writing.
• Negotiate via email: Putting your counter-proposal in writing helps you control the message, avoid pressure, and clearly list your rationales.
• Use data sources: Research real-world compensation bands using platforms like Levels.fyi (via Tech Interview Handbook) or H-1B salary databases rather than unverified general sites.
• Understand offers won't be rescinded: Major tech companies rarely revoke an offer just because you asked for more.

What to Negotiate Beyond Base Salary

Tech companies have different degrees of flexibility depending on the lever:
• Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) / Equity: Often has the most room for adjustment, especially at mid-to-senior levels where equity makes up the bulk of your total compensation.
• Sign-on Bonus: Easier for companies to approve than raising your permanent base salary. Use it to cover unvested equity or bonuses you are walking away from at your current job.
• Start Date: Time your start date to coincide with your current employer’s next stock vesting cliff to avoid leaving money on the table ("double-dipping").
• Level / Title: If you are operating at a higher scope, push for an uplevel (though this requires strong evidence or a 30-60-90 day plan).
• Non-monetary perks: Remote work flexibility, extra PTO days, or relocation assistance.

Leverage & Strategy

• Competing offers: Having another active offer is your strongest piece of leverage. Be transparent with recruiters about your interview timelines to force alignment.
• The "Reason" rule: Always back up your counter-offer with a logical rationale (e.g., total compensation alignment with market data, a competing offer, or increased responsibilities).
• Build internal advocates: Speaking with the hiring manager or skip-level manager to discuss your vision for the role can turn them into internal champions who advocate for a better offer on your behalf.
If you'd like to tailor this to your situation, tell me:
• What role/level and company type (startup vs. big tech) are you negotiating?
• Do you currently have a competing offer or unvested equity to cover?

q: ILO Generative AI and Jobs index
transcript:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) published its updated assessment in the report "Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure" (ILO Working Paper 140).

Key Findings of the Index

• Global Exposure Rate: About 24% (1 in 4) of global workers are in occupations with some level of exposure to generative AI (GenAI).
• Highest Exposure Category (Gradient 4): Only 3.3% of global employment falls into the highest exposure category where a large majority of tasks can be heavily impacted.
• Transformation vs. Replacement: The research emphasizes job transformation rather than widespread job elimination or mass redundancy, as very few occupations consist entirely of automatable tasks.
• Income Disparities: High-income countries (HICs) show a 34% total GenAI exposure rate, compared to just 11% in low-income countries (LICs), reflecting differences in economic structures and digital adoption.
• Gender Divide: Women are nearly twice as likely to hold jobs exposed to GenAI as men (roughly 29% vs. 16% across sampled countries), largely because women are more heavily represented in clerical, administrative, and routine information-processing roles.
• Most Exposed Occupations: Clerical support workers, administrative staff, secretaries, receptionists, data entry operators, and translators face the highest exposure.
• Least Exposed Occupations: Manual trades, construction, agriculture, and heavy manufacturing involve physical and non-routine tasks with very low GenAI exposure.

Methodology

• Task-Level Assessment: Evaluates nearly 30,000 to over 52,000 individual task data points across the International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08) framework.
• Four-Gradient Framework: Combines worker surveys, expert Delphi panel inputs, and large-scale AI assessments to categorize jobs into four distinct exposure gradients based on mean exposure scores and task variability.
